text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

In a surprise announcement, the 56-year-old chief executive of the ANZ Bank, Don Mercer, said yesterday he would be retiring from his position at the end of this year. His announcement came as the Bank reported an 18 percent increase in interim profit to A$615 million. Page 1.

A Federal Government proposal, which may be considered by Cabinet in the next few weeks, could see foreign investment limits for individuals lifted to 25 percent across the media industry and new rules adopted that would limit ownership to one newspaper and one television station in Sydney and Melbourne. Page 1.

An agreement which may be signed next week could see Comalco Ltd and Chevron Corp pursue the possible joint development of several projects in Queensland, including Comalco's mooted alumina refinery and Chevron's Papua New Guinea-to-Australia gas pipeline Page 25.

After announcing yesterday that the management and administration of Novacoal Pty Ltd and listed subsidiary Coal & Allied Industries Ltd would merge, Rio Tinto Energy chief executive Leigh Clifford warned the operators of the coal operations that they coud be sold off if acceptable returns are not posted within the next 12 months. Page 25.

In a move that may herald a major rationalisation of Australia's A$2 billion engineering consulting industry, United States engineering and energy services giant Brown & Root has bought the nation's biggest engineering firm, Kinhill Holdings Ltd, for A$46 million. Page 27.

New South Wales Independent Pricing and Regulatory Tribunal chairman Professor Tom Parry has released a draft determination on proposed access arrangements to the State's gas transmission system, and has slashed the tariff the Australian Gas Light Co can charge outsiders to send gas through the AGL system. Page 27
THE AUSTRALIAN

The sharemarket has reacted favourably to the news the ANZ Bank enjoyed an 18 percent surge in interim net profit to A$615 million. ANZ shares rose 18 cents to A$8.75, with chief executive Don Mercer saying the result was encouraging given the amount of competition in the industry. Page 23.

Shares in Kerry Packer's Publishing and Broadcasting Ltd lifted to a 10-year high of A$7.03 yesterday as speculation continued over the proposed takeover bid by PBL for John Fairfax Holdings Ltd. Analysts believe the proposed takeover will not go ahead if the issue becomes bogged down in politics. Page 23.

Industry sources believe up to around A$10 million worth of cigarettes may need to be destroyed by Philip Morris Australia if WD & HO Wills Holdings are successful in a Federal Court move attempting to block the sale of Philip Morris' Summit brand of cigaettes, which Wills claims is a copy of its top selling Horizon cigarettes. Page 23.

Resolute Resources chief executive Michael Carrick said yesterday an expansion of the company's two million ounce Obotan gold mine in Ghana is already being planned. As the first bar of gold was poured yesterday, annual production is expected to reach 12,000 ounces a year at a cash cost of A$280 an ounce. Page 24.

In a further cut to its steel division, BHP yesterday sought expressions of interest for its refractories business. BHP Refractories general manager Trevor Pennifold said yesterday the manufacturing part of the business, which is up for sale, turned over A$110 million a year and includes three plants in Newcastle and Wollongong. Page 25.

Bureau of Meteorology Climate Group leader Dr Neville Nicholls said in a letter to Nature yesterday that the value of Australian crops has increased by between 15 and 30 percent, which equates to A$1 billion or A$2 billion annually, due to climate change over the past 40 years. Page 25.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Savage cuts to branch numbers and staff levels have led the ANZ Bank to a surprise 18 per cent rise in half-year profit to A$615 million. The announcement of the profit produced good results in the bank's shares, which rose 18 cents, or 2 per cent, to A$8.75. Page 33.

ANZ chief executive Don Mercer will end his 12 years with the company at the end of this year, saying he was unsure why he was leaving, yet adding that he was not under any pressure from directors. His departure is the third key resignation this month, fllowing the announcements that executive director Alister Maitland and chief financial officer David Craig are also leaving. Page 33.

Stockbroking analysts, including BZW Australia analyst Nick Selvaratnam, have warned investors off buying any further shares in Colonial, as the banking and insurance group is trading nearly 15 percent over its fair-value range. The fair-value range is about A$2.80 to A$2.90, and Colonial shares have traded at a low of A$3.23, and a high of A$3.39. Page 33.

InTech Asset Consulting says superannuation funds using specialist portfolio managers will have to move quickly to avoid losing the benefit of potential higher returns. In its submission responding to a report last week by Coopers & Lybrand, InTech says such funds needed to manage the specialists on an on-going basis. Page 35.

It is understood Telecasters North Queensland TNQ.AX is the firm favourite for the float vehicle for Ten Group, with TNQ preparing to sign a memorandum of understanding with CanWest Global Communications. If the deal is approved by the Australian Broadcasting Athority and the Federal Government, CanWest's shareholding in the Ten Group will be reduced from 76 percent to 57.5 percent, with the Ten shares sold to TNQ. Page 35.

A radical report titled "regional&rural.au/for all" by the Federal Government's Information Policy Advisory Committee has called on the Government to reserve half of all new radio frequency spectrum allocations for new telecommunications companies and encourage competitors to take on Telstra in rural and regional areas. Page 35.
THE AGE

In what appears to be a rejection of the Productivity Commission's recommendation that car tariffs should be cut to 5 per cent and export incentives abandoned, Industry Minister John Moore last night reassured car industry leaders that policies for the industry would be designed to improve Australia's attraction for new investment. Page B1.

After five years in charge of the ANZ Bank, its chief executive Don Mercer announced his early retirement yesterday as the Bank reported a surprise bumper first-half profit of A$615 million. Mercer's departure will trigger a succession crisis at the Bank with there being no obvious successor to the position. Page B1.

There is now speculation over who will take over from outgoing ANZ chief executive Don Mercer, as the most obvious contender, Alister Maitland, announced his retirement as head of the Bank's international operations only a fortnight ago. Mercer is keeping quiet on his reasons for leaving the Bank, but it is believed he had confrontations with directors on several occasions. Page B1.

On the back of the release of the ANZ Bank's better-than-expected results, and the steadying of BHP after recent share losses, the Australian All Ordinaries hit another record high yesterday, closing 6.3 points higher at 2585.2. The rise follows an increase in the index of 54.5 points since May 20. Page B1.

In a Federal Court hearing yesterday, tobacco giant Philip Morris promised it would not market its new Summit brand of cigarettes pending a further hearing. The move follows a complaint by rival WD & HO Wills that the packaging copied its Horizon brand incolouring, lettering and imagery. Wills was strongly committed to defending the Horizon product, given that it is its fast-growing cigarette brand this decade. Page B1.

Singapore-based retailer World of Sports has decided to buy 19.9 percent of specialist sporting goods retailer Rebel Sport, allowing Rebel to expand its operations in South-East Asia and possibly diversify beyond its present markets. The proposed A$12.7 million purchase forms one stage of a two-part sell-down of a 28 per cent parcel of shares owned by Rebel Sport's founder and chairman Sam Linz, and non-executive director Robert Gavshorn. Page B2.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
